title.zh: 去八百英里外求援：象岛上的一次名单与取舍
title.en: Eight Hundred Miles for Help: A Crew List and Its Trade-offs on Elephant Island

dek.zh: 足额口粮只够五个星期，一条小船，六个名额。队长要说服全队走一条危险极大的路，还要否掉带病号上船的提议，并在开船前把整支队伍交到留守者手里。
dek.en: Full rations for five weeks, one small boat, six places. The leader had to talk the whole party into a voyage whose perils were extreme, veto a proposal to take a sick man along, and hand the stranded party over to the man staying behind before the boat pulled away.

paras.zh: 队长欧内斯特·沙克尔顿和他的队伍困在象岛上，最后六人乘一条小船出海求援，二十二人留在岛上。下面的经过出自他在《南方》中的第一人称自述。经过一段乘船航程后，他们粮食有限，有人冻伤，而且象岛上根本不会有人来搜寻他们。口粮按足额只够全队吃五个星期。减量可以撑三个月，或许还能靠海豹和象海豹补一些。但沙克尔顿不敢把信心全押在这上面：海滩上的海兽似乎都走了，冬天近了。燃料主要靠海兽脂肪。初步估量形势后，他决定全队每天只吃一顿热食。
paras.en: Ernest Shackleton, leader of the party, and his men were stranded on Elephant Island; in the end six sailed for help in one small boat and twenty-two stayed on the island. What follows comes from his first-person account in South. After a boat journey, their food was limited, a man was frostbitten, and there was no chance at all of any search being made for them there. At full ration the food would last the whole party five weeks. Cut back, it could be spread over three months, and would probably be supplemented to some extent by seals and sea-elephants. But Shackleton dared not count on that with full confidence: the animals seemed to have deserted the beach and winter was near. They were mainly dependent on blubber for fuel. After a preliminary survey of the situation, he decided the party must be limited to one hot meal a day.

paras.zh: 除了粮食，人的状况也令人担心。艰苦与风寒在队伍身上留下了痕迹，几名队员的健康和精神状况令人深感不安；一名队员的双脚在乘船途中冻伤，伤势很糟，两位医生担心必须动手术。
paras.en: Beyond the food, the men's condition was also a worry. Privation and exposure had left their mark on the party, and the health and mental condition of several men were causing serious anxiety. One man's feet, frostbitten during the boat journey, were in a bad way, and the two doctors feared an operation would be necessary.

paras.zh: 摆在面前的出路只有一条：派人乘小船出海求援，而且不能拖。记述里写这一句时没有回旋余地——「That conclusion was forced upon me」，这个结论是被逼出来的。
paras.en: One way out remained: take a boat for help, and do it now. The account leaves no room to maneuver — "That conclusion was forced upon me". The conclusion was forced on him.

paras.zh: 求援的去处是南乔治亚。它在八百多英里以外，但位于西风带内，东岸任何一个捕鲸站都可以指望找到捕鲸人；只要海上没有冰、小船撑得过那些巨浪，一队人乘船可望完成航行，并在一个月之内带着援助返回。
paras.en: The destination was South Georgia. It lay over eight hundred miles off, but inside the belt of the west winds, and whalers could be counted on at any of the whaling stations on its east coast. Provided the sea was clear of ice and the boat survived the great seas, a boat party might make the voyage and be back with relief within a month.

paras.zh: 出海的风险明摆着。队长算过最坏情形：这趟冒险不会给留在岛上的人增加任何风险，冬天要吃饭的嘴也少了；船上只带六人一个月的口粮——「for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under」，一个月到不了南乔治亚，就是死路。还有一条他看重的考虑：象岛上根本不会有任何搜寻队来找他们。
paras.en: The hazards of the ocean were plain, but the leader had priced the worst case. At worst the venture would add nothing to the risks of the men left on the island — there would be fewer mouths to feed through the winter — and the boat needed no more than a month's provisions for six, "for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under". And one consideration weighed with him: there was no chance at all of any search being made for them on Elephant Island.

paras.zh: 这件事必须向全队讲清楚。记述写明这个案子需要详细论证，因为所有人都知道航程的危险是极端的，风险只由援助的急迫需要来辩护。五月中，合恩角以南的海域被认为是世界上最暴虐的风暴水域，天气不稳，天色阴沉，大风几乎不停。一种解释是：他没有把出海说成上策，只说成不得已。
paras.en: The case had to be argued to the whole party in some detail, since everyone knew the journey's perils were extreme, and the risk was justified only by their urgent need of assistance. In mid-May the ocean south of Cape Horn is known to be the most tempestuous storm-swept area of water in the world: unsettled weather, dull overcast skies, gales almost unceasing. One reading is that he did not present the voyage as the best option, only the necessary one.

paras.zh: 谁去谁留，从两个要求随行的人说起：以领航见长的沃斯利（Worsley），和后来留在岛上主持队伍的怀尔德（Wild）。两人都意识到必须出海，都要求随行；队长当场告诉怀尔德他必须留下，靠他在自己离开期间把队伍拢住，并交代万一求援失败，春季带人去欺骗岛（Deception Island）。带沃斯利的理由写得很实在：队长对他作为领航员的准确与迅速评价极高，尤其在困难情况下能迅速测出并算出船位。
paras.en: Who went and who stayed began with two men who asked to come: Worsley, valued as a navigator, and Wild, who would stay on the island to hold the party together. Both realized the attempt must be made, and both asked to accompany him. The leader told Wild at once that he must stay — to hold the party together during the absence and, if the rescue failed, to take the men to Deception Island in the spring. His reason for taking Worsley was practical: "a very high opinion of his accuracy and quickness as a navigator, and especially in the snapping and working out of positions in difficult circumstances".

paras.zh: 还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。他召集众人，说明计划，征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来。克林（Crean）原本被安排留在岛上当怀尔德的帮手，他恳求随行，与怀尔德商量之后，队长答应带上他。记述里也写了挑人的考虑：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。
paras.en: Four more were needed. He decided to call for volunteers while noting that he already had a pretty good idea of his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". He called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers; many came forward at once. Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The account also sets out his criteria: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.

paras.zh: 两位医生麦基尔罗伊（McIlroy）和麦克林（Macklin）都想随行，但明白自己的职责是留在岛上照顾病号。两位医生提议把双脚冻伤的布莱克博罗（Blackborrow）带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活；他看不出一个躺在舱底、动弹不得的病人，怎么可能熬过必定会遇到的坏天气。
paras.en: The two doctors, McIlroy and Macklin, were both anxious to go but realized that their duty lay on the island with the sick men. The doctors suggested taking Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and he did not see how a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could possibly survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.

paras.zh: 名单最后定为沃斯利、克林、麦克尼什（McNeish）、麦卡锡（McCarthy）、文森特（Vincent）和队长本人六人。另一件事是加固小船：队长把木匠（他也在这六人之中）叫来，请他想办法让小船更耐风浪；木匠先问自己是不是随行的人，听说「Yes」显得相当高兴。他年过五十，身体不算好。
paras.en: The list closed at six: Worsley, Crean, McNeish, McCarthy, Vincent, and the leader himself. A separate matter was strengthening the boat: the leader called the carpenter (he was one of the six) and asked whether he could do anything to make the boat more seaworthy; the carpenter's first question was whether he was going along, and hearing "Yes," he seemed quite pleased. He was over fifty and not altogether fit.

paras.zh: 小船的加固是拼凑而成的，很简陋，但足以给一层帆布覆罩打底。帆布冻得硬邦邦，只能先裁好，再在脂肪炉上一英尺一英尺地烤开，才能缝成覆罩，最后钉好、拧紧。覆罩装上后确实给了小船一层安全的样子，可队长心里不踏实，觉得它「bore a strong likeness to stage scenery」——看着像花岗石墙，其实不过是帆布和板条。事后证明，这层覆罩确实顶用。
paras.en: The work on the boat was a patched-up affair, but it provided a base for a canvas covering. The canvas came frozen stiff; it had to be cut and then thawed over the blubber stove foot by foot before it could be sewn into a cover, then nailed and screwed into position. The cover did lend the boat an appearance of safety, but the leader felt uneasy that "it bore a strong likeness to stage scenery" — a wall that looks like granite and is in fact no better than canvas and lath. As events proved, the covering served its purpose well.

paras.zh: 队长与沃斯利、怀尔德登上临海的岩顶，从比海滩更好的位置察看冰情；外面的浮冰带看来已碎得足够，他决定除非条件不允许，次日早晨乘詹姆斯·凯尔德号（James Caird）出发。浮冰随时可能合拢。决定做出后，队长用当天余下的时间检查船、装备和物资，并与沃斯利、怀尔德商量计划。在象岛坚实陆地上的最后一夜又冷又不舒服。开船前，队长乘小艇上岸，与留守并全权指挥的怀尔德作最后交代：交代万一求援失败他该怎么做，同时几乎把整个局面和行动、决定的范围都交给怀尔德自行判断，「I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment」，并告诉他把队伍托付给他，随后向众人道别。升帆解缆向东北而去时，留在岸上的人在海边站成可怜的一小群，背后是岛上冷硬的高地，脚下的海在翻涌；他们挥手，喊了三声欢呼。
paras.en: Worsley, Wild and the leader climbed to the summit of the seaward rocks to examine the ice from a better vantage-point than the beach offered. The belt of pack outside appeared sufficiently broken, and he decided that, unless conditions forbade it, they would start in the James Caird the following morning. The pack might close at any time. With that decision made, the leader spent the rest of the day looking over the boat, gear and stores, and discussing plans with Worsley and Wild. The last night on the solid ground of Elephant Island was cold and uncomfortable. Before casting off, the leader went ashore for a final word with Wild, who remained in full command: directions for what to do if no help came, and then, in his words, "I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment". He told Wild he trusted the party to him and said goodbye to the men. With the jib set and the painter cut, they stood away to the north-east. Those left behind made a pathetic little group on the beach, grim heights at their backs and the sea seething at their feet — but they waved and gave three hearty cheers.

paras.zh: 船上的日子从细节开始磨人。做饭要三个人：一人护灯，两人护铝锅——锅得随时从炉子上提开，免得船一晃出事；灯也要挡水，浪花不断从船头打过来，那层覆罩并不防水。人都挤在覆罩底下，贴着箱子和压舱物找角度躺跪；虽不舒服，但没有这层覆罩根本没法做饭。出海第六天早上，船被夜里结的冰压得失去弹性，不再随浪抬起，像根圆木。先扔掉冻在船侧的备用桨，留两支靠岸用；再扔掉两条湿透冻硬的毛皮睡袋（各约四十磅）。值下班的有三个人，与其用体温去焐冻硬的睡袋，不如钻进别人刚腾出的湿睡袋。剩下四条，三条在用，一条留给有人彻底垮掉时应急。
paras.en: Life aboard wore men down in details. Cooking needed three: one to hold the lamp, two to guard the aluminium pot, which had to be lifted clear of the Primus stove whenever a lurch threatened disaster; the lamp needed shielding from water, since spray came over the bows and the flimsy decking was by no means watertight. All of it happened in the cramped space beneath the decking, men lying or kneeling and wedging themselves against cases and ballast — uncomfortable, though without the decking they could not have cooked at all. On the morning of the sixth day the boat lost her resiliency and stopped rising to the seas, weighed down by ice that had formed overnight: more log than boat. The spare oars, frozen to her sides, went overboard, two kept for inshore work. Two fur sleeping-bags followed — soaked through, probably forty pounds each, frozen stiff. With three men in the watch below, it was better to turn into a wet bag just vacated by another man than to thaw a frozen one with body heat. Four bags were left: three in use, one held back in case a man broke down for good.

paras.zh: 有一天上午 11 点前后，缆绳断了，海锚丢失，船突然横落进浪谷，向下风漂去。那是不必冒险在大风中升帆也能让船头顶浪的唯一手段，连同宝贵的绳子都找不回来，只能敲掉帆上的冰，升帆赌它撑得住。航程中一次测算显示：已走 380 多英里，接近南乔治亚的一半。看样子能撑过去。
paras.en: About 11 a.m. one day the painter parted and the sea-anchor went — the only means of keeping the boat's head up to the seas without the risk of hoisting sail in a gale, lost along with the valuable rope. She suddenly fell off into the trough of the sea and drifted to leeward. They beat the ice off the frozen canvas and hoisted it, trusting it to hold. One reckoning showed over 380 miles done, getting on for half-way to South Georgia. It looked as though they were going to get through.

paras.zh: 航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。文森特在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比麦卡锡更能吃苦，而麦卡锡没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害。队长不肯增加配给，因为万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天；有人恳求预支第二天的水，他也坚决拒绝。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。5月8日中午12点30分，麦卡锡从云隙中望见南乔治亚的黑色悬崖，距离开象岛整十四天。但岩岸看似直落入海，夜色将近，天气征兆也不好，那时贸然登陆无异自杀，只能离岸停驶，等待天亮。次日清晨风向转为西北，迅速增强为他们所有人经历过的最猛的飓风之一，风浪把船推向海岸，他们无能为力。直到天黑后风向突然转变，他们才得以重新驶离海岸；大风刚缓，锁住桅杆的销钉就掉了出来——队长写道，飓风中它若脱落，谁也救不了他们。5月10日，他们驶向一处队长认为必定是哈康国王湾（King Haakon Bay）的大海湾；风向转为从湾内吹出，他们在强风中抢风五次，才穿过礁石进入宽阔的湾口。暮色将近，他们转向海湾南岸一处有礁石护着的小湾。小船乘着涌浪触到海滩，几分钟后众人都平安上了岸；他们在脚边发现一条淡水溪流，随即跪下大口痛饮。但上岸并不等于求援成功：冰川和陡峭的山坡挡住了从小湾进入内陆的路，他们还得驶向海湾顶端，而指望找到捕鲸人的捕鲸站在东岸。登陆那晚，众人往岸上爬时詹姆斯·凯尔德号船尾重重撞击，舵被撞掉了，在海滩和够得着的岩石间仔细搜寻也没找到，这是严重的损失。小船又因割去舷板而变弱，走海路离斯特罗姆内斯（Stromness）捕鲸站仍有150英里；另一条路是尝试横越岛屿，而象岛上还有二十二人在等待只有他们才能带去的援救。
paras.en: At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst. The leader would not raise the allowance, since an unfavourable wind might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days; when he was begged to let anyone draw against the morrow's allowance, he firmly refused. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure. At 12.30 p.m. on May 8, McCarthy caught a glimpse of the black cliffs of South Georgia through a rift in the clouds, just fourteen days after leaving Elephant Island. But the rocky coast seemed to drop sheer to the sea, night was drawing near and the weather signs were unfavourable; to have attempted a landing then would have been suicidal, so they hauled off and hove to, waiting for dawn. Early the next morning the wind shifted to the north-west and quickly rose to one of the worst hurricanes any of them had ever experienced; wind and sea were driving them ashore, and they could do nothing. Only after dark did the wind suddenly shift and leave them free to make an offing again; almost as soon as the gale eased, the pin that locked the mast to the thwart fell out — had it gone during the hurricane, the leader writes, nothing could have saved them. On May 10 they made for a big indentation the leader thought must be King Haakon Bay; with the wind blowing out of the bay, they tacked five times in the strong wind before getting through the reef into the wide mouth of the bay. With dusk approaching, they turned toward a small cove guarded by a reef on the south side of the bay. The boat ran in on a swell and touched the beach, and in a few minutes they were all safe ashore; finding a stream of fresh water almost at their feet, they were soon down on their knees drinking. But landing was not the same as securing relief: glaciers and precipitous mountain slopes barred the way inland from the cove, they still had to sail to the head of the sound, and the whaling stations where whalers could be counted on lay on the east coast. On the night of the landing, as the James Caird bumped heavily astern while they scrambled ashore, the rudder was knocked off, and a careful search of the beach and the rocks within reach failed to find it — a serious loss. The boat had also been weakened by the cutting away of the topsides, and they were still 150 miles from Stromness whaling station by sea; the alternative was to attempt the crossing of the island, while twenty-two men on Elephant Island waited for the relief that only they could secure.

paras.zh: 把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，一个月到不了南乔治亚就必死无疑，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。据作者序言，留在象岛的二十二人在那里勉强熬了四个半月，远超当初一个月内带援助返回的预期。同一篇序言写道，营救经过不止一次尝试，最终由智利政府直接促成，帕尔多（Luis Pardo）指挥的耶尔乔号（Yelcho）完成了最后一次、成功的营救。本文不据此推出因果评价。本文推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。
paras.en: Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they did not make South Georgia within the month, they were sure to go under. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. According to the author's preface, the twenty-two men left on Elephant Island eked out a bare existence there for four and a half months, far beyond the hoped-for return with relief within a month. The same preface says the relief took more than one attempt, and that the Chilean Government was directly responsible for the rescue, with the Yelcho under Captain Luis Pardo making the last and successful venture. This piece draws no causal verdict from that. This piece infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.

paras.zh: 拒绝病号上船那一条，读起来最不舒服，但记录里给的是存活推断，不是道德立场：健康的人在船上都难活，在他看来，躺在舱底、动弹不得的病人熬不过坏天气。本文推断，这种取舍的难处不在决定本身，而在它必须给出理由——两位医生提了建议，被否掉了，记述里写明了否决的理由。
paras.en: The refusal of the sick man is the least comfortable paragraph to read, yet the record offers survival reasoning rather than a moral stance: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and in his view a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not survive the heavy weather. This piece infers that the difficulty of such a trade-off lies less in the decision itself than in having to give reasons for it: the two doctors made a proposal, it was vetoed, and the account sets down why.

paras.zh: 还有一处值得留意：记述说他决定征求志愿者，同时心里基本知道会选谁。原文写明，他召集众人、说明计划、征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来；但最终的人选仍由他选定。本文提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式。一种解释是：先向全队说明计划、详细讲清危险和理由，再征求志愿，可能让名单读起来更像共识而不是指派。这只是本文的解释。
paras.en: One more detail catches the eye: the account says he decided to call for volunteers while already having a pretty good idea of his choices. The original states that he called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers, and that many came forward at once; yet the final selection was still his. One alternative this piece raises would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. One reading is that explaining the plan and arguing the dangers and reasons to the party in detail before asking for volunteers may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. This is only this piece's reading.

paras.zh: 今天，资源有限、外部不会主动来救的小团队会遇到同一类问题。一个只有几个人的偏远工作站，补给只够再撑一段时间，通讯断了，下一班补给不知何时到：是全员留下硬撑，还是派人冒险出去求援？先算最坏情形——出去的人会不会让留下的人更糟？定量能砍到什么程度，又能把可撑的时间延长多少？
paras.en: Small teams short of resources, with no outside rescue coming, face the same question. A remote station of a few people, supplies good for another stretch of time, communications down, the next resupply date unknown: does everyone stay and endure, or does someone go out and risk seeking help? Start with the worst case: does sending people out make matters worse for those who stay? How far can rations be cut, and how much longer would that let them hold out?

paras.zh: 第二类问题是临走前怎么交班。负责人要同时交出两样东西：失败时的后手——到某个时点没消息就换方案；以及现场的判断范围。只交代步骤不给判断权，留守的人会事事等消息；只说“你看着办”却不讲失败的下场，责任就悬在半空。
paras.en: The second problem is the handover before departure. A leader must hand over two things at once: the fallback if the attempt fails — no word by a certain point, then switch plans — and the scope of judgment on the ground. Steps without judgment leave those behind waiting for instructions on everything; "use your own judgment" without spelling out what failure looks like leaves responsibility hanging in mid-air.

paras.zh: 本文只依据沙克尔顿《南方》中他事后写下的第一人称自述。作者说，南乔治亚航程的记述依据逐日写下的简略笔记，笔记通常只记距离、船位和天气，航程中的具体经过则来自记忆。文中的对话都带有记述性质：把队伍托付给怀尔德的那句交代、克林恳求随行，都未必是逐字原话。队长自述看队员时信心在增加，那是回忆中的自我描述，不是当时可核实的心理记录。
paras.en: This piece relies only on Shackleton's first-person account in South, written after the fact. The author says the account of the voyage to South Georgia is based on scanty notes made day by day, which usually dealt with the bare facts of distances, positions and weather, while the incidents themselves came from memory. Its dialogue is reported, not transcribed — the words entrusting the party to Wild, Crean's plea for a place in the boat — and need not be verbatim. The leader's statement that his confidence grew as he looked at the men is retrospective self-description, not a verifiable record of his state of mind at the time.

paras.zh: 有一处要留白：文森特为什么垮掉，队长自己说难以解释，本文不替他补心理。正文的天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日；距离、口粮、水的数字都照原文：八百多英里、三百八十多英里、半品脱。原文是扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文写法。
paras.en: One blank stays blank. Why Vincent collapsed, the leader himself says he could not easily account for, and this piece supplies no psychology for him. The only day counts kept in the text are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, both stated explicitly in the original, and dates follow the original: May 8 and May 10; distances, rations and water figures follow the original: over eight hundred miles, over three hundred and eighty miles, half a pint. The source is a scanned, text-recognized print, with occasional garbled words; quotations follow it as printed.

scenario.zh: 五个人的小团队，账上只够发四个月工资，产品不上线就没有收入；其中两个人是唯一能对外谈事的人。要不要派人出去找钱、找渠道，谁去谁留？
scenario.en: A five-person team with only four months of payroll left in the bank and no revenue until the product ships; two of the five are the only ones who can negotiate with the outside world. Do you send someone out to raise money and open channels — and who goes, who stays?

question.zh: 当所有选项都很糟时，什么样的最坏情形算法能让人自愿跟从？把它讲得太清楚，会不会反而没人敢去？
question.en: When every option is bad, what kind of worst-case arithmetic makes people willing to follow? And does spelling it out too clearly risk frightening everyone off the attempt?

assumptions.zh: 团队五人；现金够四个月；外部不会主动注资；两人有对外谈判能力，另外三人维持产品；失败意味着全部投入归零。
assumptions.en: Five people; cash for four months; no outside funding will arrive uninvited; two can negotiate externally while three keep the product moving; failure means losing everything invested.

steps.zh: 先算最坏情形：出去的人不增加留守者的开支，反而少一份开销；给出去的人定明确的时限与物资上限（例如一个月、只带够一个月开销的钱），超时即默认失败；说清楚：之所以冒这个险，只因为确实急需外援；公开征求意愿，但事先想好人选；离开前交代失败时的后手，并把现场判断权交给留守负责人。
steps.en: Compute the worst case first: the person who goes adds nothing to the burn of those who stay, and in fact removes one salary's worth of cost. Set a hard time limit and a supply cap for the trip (say, a month, carrying only a month of expenses), with silence past the deadline counted as failure. State plainly that the risk is being taken only because outside help is urgently needed. Ask for volunteers in the open, with the choices already thought through. Before leaving, hand over the fallback for failure, and delegate real judgment to the person staying behind.

alternative.zh: 本文提出的一种替代：不派人出去，全员接零活维持现金流。好处是短期内不分散人力，代价是没有人去打开外部通道，四个月后仍然没有援手。
alternative.en: One alternative this piece raises: send nobody out, and have everyone take contract work to keep cash flowing. The gain is that no one is pulled off the front line in the short term; the cost is that no one opens an outside channel, and after four months there is still no help.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文只依据沙克尔顿（当事人）事后的第一人称自述《南方》；航程部分据其逐日简略笔记（多为距离、船位、天气）与回忆写成；对话与心理均为记述性内容，未必逐字，本文未对照其他当事人的记录核实；天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日；距离、口粮、水的数字照原文写法；原文为扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece relies only on Shackleton's own first-person account, South, written afterwards by a participant; the voyage section was written from scanty day-by-day notes (mostly distances, positions and weather) together with memory. Dialogue and psychology are reported rather than transcribed, need not be verbatim, and have not been checked here against other participants' accounts; the only day counts used are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, as stated in the original, and dates follow the original (May 8 and May 10); distances, rations and water figures follow the original wording; the source is a scanned print in OCR, with individual words occasionally garbled, and quotations follow it as printed.
